title: Every mind different (Berakhot 58a)
hook: seeing a great crowd, one blesses the One who knows each heart
tomorrow: who baked your bread before you were even awake?

segments.voice: Yesterday, three things restore: a sound, a sight, a smell, and a scattered mind comes home. Today, a whole room full of minds.
screen: `THREE THINGS RESTORE.` → `A ROOM FULL OF MINDS.`

segments.voice: From the wings of a stage, a full house looks like one thing. A dark shape, a single cough, one big laugh. A stadium does the same, or a packed train at rush hour: the crowd. So what blessing fits a sea of faces? The Talmud has one ready. When you see a great crowd of Israel, you say: blessed is the Wise of secrets. And it gives the reason in one breath.
screen: `A FULL HOUSE, ONE SHAPE.` → `A SEA OF FACES.` → `BLESSED IS THE WISE OF SECRETS.`

segments.voice: The reason: because their minds are not like one another, and their faces are not like one another. The crowd only looks like one thing from far away. God, the blessing says, knows the secret inside every one of them, which is exactly what the person watching can't. That's why it's called the Wise of secrets. Now honesty about scope. This blessing in Berakhot is said over a great crowd of the Jewish people. But the Mishnah, in another tractate, Sanhedrin, says something wider about every human being. Why was humanity created from a single person? So that no one could say to another, my ancestor is greater than yours. And to show God's greatness: a person stamps many coins with one seal and they all come out alike. God stamped every human with the seal of the first human, and not one is like another. Put the two together, and here's what you could tell a friend tonight. One family, so no one ranks their ancestors above anyone else's. Every face different, so no one is just part of the blob. Alike enough to be family, different enough that each one is a secret. That's the crowd at a ballgame, a bus stop, a hallway between classes.
screen: `NO TWO MINDS, NO TWO FACES.` · `GOD KNOWS EACH SECRET.` · `ONE ANCESTOR, SO NO ONE RANKS.` · `ONE SEAL, NO TWO ALIKE.` · then, large: `EVERY MIND DIFFERENT.`

segments.voice: Close your eyes and bring back a crowd you were part of this week: a hallway, a store, a bus. Let three faces come into focus, one at a time. For each, notice: a whole mind I'll never fully see, from the same first family as me.
screen: `A CROWD FROM THIS WEEK.` · `THREE FACES, ONE AT A TIME.` · `A WHOLE MIND, SAME FAMILY.`

segments.voice: Every mind different: why the Talmud blesses the Wise of secrets over a crowd, the One who knows what no watcher can.
For the next crowd you're in: every mind different, every face from the same first family. Thirty-seven of fifty.

screen: `DAY 1524 COUNTS.` → `BERAKHOT · 37 OF 50.` → `TOMORROW: WHO BAKED YOUR BREAD BEFORE YOU WOKE?`

howItsDone: Jewish law gives a blessing on seeing a great crowd of Jews: 'Blessed… Wise of secrets' (chacham ha-razim); the Mishnah in Sanhedrin 4:5 teaches that every human descends from one person and that no two are alike.

chat.meaning: Seeing a great crowd, the Talmud blesses the Wise of secrets, because no two minds or faces in it are alike (Berakhot 58a).

Wise of secrets.meaning: God's name in the blessing over a great crowd

Sanhedrin.meaning: a tractate about courts; it holds the one-seal teaching

Mishnah.meaning: the early collection of Jewish law the Talmud discusses

sources.ref: Babylonian Talmud, Berakhot 58a (one who sees crowds of Israel says 'Blessed… Wise of secrets', for their minds and faces are not alike)
Mishnah Sanhedrin 4:5 (humanity created from one person so no one says 'my ancestor is greater'; one seal, no two alike)
